title: Stop prefetch-isolation oscillation causing cross-tenant starvation and long-context tail
creator: Priya Nair
description: Multiple enterprise customers operating mixed-hosting workloads (Hosted + Dedicated + Private) reported recurring escalations: sustained microbursts of long-context requests trigger a prefetch-isolation oscillation in the continuous batcher that cascades into eviction storms, admission starvation for short requests, and a pronounced 95th/99th token tail in generation latency. The behavior shows up across regions but is most visible on Dedicated pools with mixed tenant profiles. This ticket tracks a targeted production fix plus a short-term mitigation to stop customer-facing outages while we validate a longer-term admission/eviction redesign.
reproducer_steps: 1) Run a mixed workload with 80% short (<=32 tokens) requests and 20% long (>=2048 tokens) requests targeted at the same host pool
2) Enable continuous-batching with prefetch enabled and default eviction thresholds
3) Observe KV cache churn and an oscillation pattern where prefetch pods enter a quarantine state, causing inflight window shrinkage and repeated eviction waves
4) Notice short request latency spikes (P95->P99) and queue-starvation events logged against shortflow tenant metrics
impact_observed: Sustained P99 token latency increases (2-6x) for short requests during waves
Tenant-level throughput drop for latency-sensitive customers (observed 30-70% reduction)
Multiple Customer Success escalations tracked over the past 3 weeks, two SRE incident pages opened
mitigation_actions: Hotpatch (deployed) - introduce a shortflow-immortalize flag: requests tagged as short (<=64 tokens) are guaranteed a lightweight admission reserve to prevent prefetch-driven starvation
Adjust eviction hysteresis on Dedicated pools: double the hysteresis window for 10 minutes after a high-eviction burst detected
Enable per-host prefetch damping: when prefetch_quarantine_events > threshold, linearly reduce prefetch concurrency instead of full quarantine
Emergency rollout of a targeted autoscaler rule to add temporary Dedicated slots to noisy hosts while investigating
design_decisions: Move from binary prefetch quarantine to a graded dampening model with per-tenant budget tokens
Introduce an inflight reservation token pool for shortflows to make admission latency-safe during eviction churn
Decouple KV commit pressure from admission windows by introducing deferred-kv-commit that delays non-critical KV writes during eviction storms
Keep the default behavior conservative for Hosted customers; Dedicated customers can opt into aggressive prefetch to maximize throughput once stable
acceptance_criteria: Shortflow P95 and P99 return to baseline within 10 minutes of mitigation when replayed with synthetic mixed load
No more customer escalations citing starvation related to this oscillation in the next 14 days for impacted clusters
New telemetry shows prefetch damping reduces quarantine repeats by >= 80%
E2E regression tests added to CI exercising mixed-hosting admission/eviction scenarios
rollout_plan: Canary: runtime-1.19 canary host pool in us-west-2 with telemetry guardrails - 1 hour
Gradual: expand to 10% of Dedicated capacity over 6 hours if no regressions
Full: 100% Dedicated and Private pools within 48 hours conditional on stability
Fallback: automatic rollback if shortflow P99 latency increases > 2x or eviction_count spikes
postmortem_notes: Root cause: tight coupling between prefetch quarantine state and admission window shrink logic - one causes the other in a feedback loop
Contributing factors: eviction thresholds tuned for homogeneous long-context workloads, not mixed-hosting; lack of shortflow admission reserve
Preventive controls: automated detection rule for quarantine oscillation and a runbook to patch host-level damping as a hotfix
